name: DevOps
certifications: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer

beginner.summary: For developers, testers and system administrators who are new to DevOps practice and want to see how one change travels from a laptop to a running service. The course follows a single sample service, orders-api (a small Python web API with pytest tests), through the whole delivery path: DevOps culture and the CALMS model, value stream mapping, Linux and shell work, team branching and pull requests, build automation, a first CI pipeline in GitHub Actions, unit tests and coverage, artifacts and semantic versioning, container images and registries, a first continuous delivery to a test environment, configuration and secrets, infrastructure as code concepts, monitoring and logs, and team collaboration. Dedicated courses cover each tool in depth; here the focus is how the pieces fit together, ending in a capstone that takes the app from commit to running service.
prerequisites: Has written and run small programs in any language and can read simple Python code
Uses a terminal to change directories, run commands and edit text files
Has a laptop with rights to install Git, Docker Desktop or Docker Engine, kind and kubectl, plus a free GitHub account
outcomes: Explain DevOps with the CALMS model and map a delivery value stream with lead time and wait time
Build a CI pipeline that lints, tests, versions and packages a service as a container image on every push
Deliver the image automatically to a test environment with configuration and secrets kept out of the code
Monitor the delivered service with health checks, metrics, logs and an alert, and trace a failed delivery to its cause

intermediate.summary: For engineers who already run a working CI pipeline and a first automated deployment and now need delivery that is fast, safe and measurable for a team. Using orders-api, a second service and a local kind cluster, the course covers trunk-based development and feature flags, pipeline design and quality gates, the test pyramid inside a pipeline, DevSecOps with SAST, software composition analysis, secrets scanning and container scanning, environment promotion, rolling, blue-green and canary releases, a GitOps workflow with Argo CD, infrastructure pipelines with OPA policy checks, Kubernetes delivery, observability-driven releases, incident response with postmortems, and DORA metrics. Each tool appears as an example of a practice; dedicated courses go deeper on each one.
prerequisites: Has built a CI workflow in GitHub Actions or GitLab CI that tests code and pushes a container image
Can deploy and inspect a workload on Kubernetes with kubectl apply, get, describe and logs

outcomes: Design a pipeline with stages, caching, reusable workflows and quality gates that keeps feedback under 10 minutes
